note: One registry for every free plan the ZIKR project relies on. Limits are copied from the vendor's own page (source field). Usage is never invented: a service with no recorded usage reports 'unknown' until a real number is entered.

services.name: Supabase database size
services.resetNote: Not a rolling window: size is measured live. Writes fail once the project is over quota.
services.fallback: Keep large immutable text (tafsir, hadith bodies, Quran text) in the static offline bundle already in the repo and load it from the CDN instead of Postgres; archive finished rows.
services.notes: 114 surahs, 6236 ayahs plus tafsir and 2964 hadiths live here. This is the most likely free limit to be hit first.

services.name: Supabase file storage
services.resetNote: Measured live; deleting files frees space immediately.
services.fallback: Cloudflare R2 free tier (10 GB, zero egress) for bulk media; Supabase Storage only for small authenticated files.
services.notes: Audio and images are the volume here, not database rows.

services.name: Supabase egress
services.resetNote: Monthly billing cycle.
services.fallback: Serve media from a CDN with free egress (Cloudflare R2) and cache API responses at the edge.

services.name: Supabase edge function invocations
services.resetNote: Monthly billing cycle.
services.fallback: Move the prayer scheduler to a GitHub Actions cron if invocations climb.

services.name: Supabase monthly active users
services.resetNote: Monthly.
services.fallback: No action needed at current scale.

services.name: Supabase active projects
services.resetNote: Paused projects do not count as active.
services.fallback: Keep one production project plus at most one staging project; pause staging when idle.

services.name: Days since the last database activity
services.resetNote: A free project pauses after one week with no activity.
services.fallback: A scheduled keep-alive read every 3 days (GitHub Actions cron) keeps the project awake at zero cost.
services.notes: A countdown, not consumption: the number must stay under 7, so a 3-day keep-alive is enough.

services.name: Vercel fast data transfer
services.resetNote: Monthly allotment on Hobby.
services.fallback: Serve large media from Cloudflare R2 (zero egress) so page HTML and API traffic stay small.
services.notes: Media files, not HTML, are what would push this.

services.name: Vercel CDN requests
services.resetNote: Monthly allotment on Hobby.
services.fallback: Cache static assets long (already done) and cut per-page request count.

services.name: Vercel function invocations
services.resetNote: Monthly allotment on Hobby.
services.fallback: Cache API routes and prefer static or ISR rendering for public pages.

services.name: Vercel deployments per day
services.resetNote: Rolling daily limit; exceeding it blocks deploys until the next day.
services.fallback: Batch merges and deploy on purpose instead of on every push.

services.name: Vercel build time per deployment
services.resetNote: Per deployment cap; a longer build fails.
services.fallback: Keep the Next build lean; run heavy checks in CI rather than in the build.

services.name: Vercel static file upload per deployment
services.resetNote: Per deployment.
services.fallback: Move large binaries out of the repo to R2 or Cloudinary; the 4.5 MB adhan audio should not ship in the build.

services.name: Cloudinary credits
services.resetNote: Monthly credit reset.
services.fallback: Next/Image already resizes on demand, so transformations can drop to zero; move bulk files to Supabase Storage or R2.
services.notes: Credits are shared across storage, transformations and bandwidth, so one large upload can eat a month.

services.name: GitHub Actions compute minutes
services.resetNote: Monthly per billing account. Standard runners are unlimited for public repositories.
services.fallback: Reduce cron frequency, cap batch size per run, cancel superseded runs, or run the heavy video job on his own machine.
services.notes: The repo is private, so minutes are metered. Publishing it would remove the limit but expose the code.

services.name: Hugging Face ZeroGPU generations per day
services.resetNote: Free ZeroGPU quota is per user per day. PRO adds 8x quota and queue priority, which this project does not need.
services.fallback: The local FFmpeg template renderer needs no quota; the provider router already falls through to it.
services.notes: 6 is our own ceiling, set below the observed free daily quota so a run never dies mid-queue.

services.name: Google Flow credits
services.resetNote: Refreshes daily, observed around 6:20 AM Cairo.
services.fallback: Local upscale of the free 720p download with scripts/upscale-video.mjs instead of buying 1080p or 4K.
services.notes: Observed 2026-11-28 on the signed-in account: 47 to 37 credits for one 8 second 720p clip (10 credits); 720p download free, 1080p and 4K downloads tagged Upgrade. A free day is 4 clips with 10 credits left.

services.name: Resend emails per day
services.resetNote: Daily cap on the free plan.
services.fallback: In-app admin queue alerts already exist; email is the optional second channel.

services.name: Resend emails per month
services.resetNote: Monthly.
services.fallback: Supabase Auth sends sign-in mail; Resend stays for admin alerts only.

services.name: YouTube Data API quota units
services.resetNote: Resets at midnight Pacific Time.
services.fallback: The cached channel feed already serves pages when the quota is exhausted.

services.name: YouTube uploads per day
services.resetNote: videos.insert has its own bucket of 100 per day.
services.fallback: Queue surplus for the next day; the publishing queue already retries.

services.name: Gemini API requests (free-only mode)
services.resetNote: Production runs with VIDEO_FREE_ONLY=true, so this must stay at zero.
services.fallback: Template renderer and static content; no AI call is required for the site to work.
services.notes: A limit of 0 is a guard, not a quota: any usage means the free-only switch was bypassed.

services.name: Public Nominatim request rate
services.resetNote: Usage policy: at most one request per second, no bulk geocoding, identifying User-Agent required.
services.fallback: Cache geocoding results in the database; self-host Nominatim if volume grows.

services.name: Cloudflare R2 storage (planned)
services.resetNote: Monthly free allowance; egress is free at any volume.
services.fallback: Not in use yet. This is the escape hatch for Supabase Storage and Vercel bandwidth.

services.name: Cloudflare R2 Class A operations (planned)
services.resetNote: Monthly.
services.fallback: Writes are rare; reads dominate and use the Class B allowance.

services.name: Cloudflare R2 Class B operations (planned)
services.resetNote: Monthly.
services.fallback: Put a CDN cache in front so repeat reads never reach the bucket.

video.quotaBackoff: On a quota or 429 error from a provider, mark that provider unavailable for the rest of the local day and fall through to the next one; the template renderer always works.
video.upscale: Render at 720p, then upscale locally with scripts/upscale-video.mjs when a platform needs 1080p. Never buy Flow's 1080p or 4K download.
